definitions.explanation: The Christian cross or crucifix as a religious symbol. Also refers to the physical object.
Used figuratively to mean a heavy burden or responsibility that one must endure.

examples.japanese: {教会|きょうかい}の{上|うえ}に{十字架|じゅうじか}がある。
examples.english: There is a cross on top of the church.

examples.japanese: {首|くび}から{十字架|じゅうじか}のネックレスを{下|さ}げている。
examples.english: She is wearing a cross necklace around her neck.

examples.japanese: キリストは{十字架|じゅうじか}にかけられたと{伝|つた}えられている。
examples.english: It is said that Christ was crucified on the cross.

examples.japanese: その{過去|かこ}は{彼|かれ}にとって{重|おも}い{十字架|じゅうじか}だ。
examples.english: That past is a heavy cross for him to bear.

examples.japanese: {責任者|せきにんしゃ}として、その{失敗|しっぱい}の{十字架|じゅうじか}を{背負|せお}い{続|つづ}けている。
examples.english: As the person in charge, he continues to bear the cross of that failure.

examples.japanese: あの{事故|じこ}は{一生|いっしょう}の{十字架|じゅうじか}になるだろう。
examples.english: That accident will be a cross to bear for a lifetime.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 1 is the literal religious object. Sense 2 is a figurative extension meaning a heavy burden or guilt, similar to the English expression "cross to bear." The figurative use is common in literary and dramatic contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {十字架|じゅうじか}を{背負|せお}う (to bear a cross; to carry a burden)
- {十字架|じゅうじか}にかける (to crucify)
- {十字架|じゅうじか}{像|ぞう} (crucifix statue)
